memo.verdict: Bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction medium-low, a working hypothesis until the FY2026 results of 23 Feb 2027. The park rule is applied and not triggered: management (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) B; business quality (E 2, BB 2) B; predictability (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) B; trackability (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) C. The case is a good business bought cheap ahead of a demanding half-year, to be progressed and watched, not sized. Entry condition named: at 217p the eighteen-month path clears the 20 percent bar by a hair and the three-year path does not; below about 200p both do; the November 2026 trading update is the last read before the print. The February print decides whether the case is a B to be built or a C to be parked: if the sector's re-basing is permanent and the H2 2026 margin bridge is missed, the case is a C and belongs parked.
case: The thesis in the record's words: Convatec is a solid recurring-consumables business whose second act, 6 to 8 percent organic growth and a 24 to 26 percent margin by 2027, is priced as if it had already failed; at 217.0p the shares trade at 11.6x the earnings two years out, the lowest multiple of five years, so the cash and the earnings alone pay about 14 percent a year and the odds-weighted return is about 21 percent if one demanding half-year is delivered; the case turns on the FY2026 results of 23 Feb 2027.

- The change forces are internal, mature and still working; the external backdrop is a mild headwind. Internal forces pass the framework's screen: mid-term guidance raised (6 to 8 percent organic from 2027, 24 to 26 percent margin by 2027); standards lifted (G&A from 13 percent of sales in 2019 to 6 percent in H1 2026; 130 basis points of productivity in H1 2026; lines needing two operators instead of ten; a fourth shared-service centre in Hyderabad late 2026); sixteen launches in three waves (Wave 1 over half of H1 2026 organic growth; Esteem Body $60m annualised run-rate and 15 percent of its segment; ConvaFoam about 6 percent global foam share toward 10 percent, winning over 50 percent of US evaluations; GentleCath Air for Women more than doubled; ConvaNiox on the UK Drug Tariff at £40 a dressing); $500m of buybacks across 2025 and 2026 after none in 2021 to 2023. But it is the second act of a program running since 2019, so most of its output is already in the numbers; the chief executive change is a continuity succession and the finance seat is vacant. 'Internal forces' B; 'External forces' C; 'Change Forces' C.

- External forces net to a mild headwind: demand structural and slow at 4 to 5 percent a year (advanced wound care about $6.0bn, ostomy $3.7bn, continence $2.4bn, infusion about $1bn; the global wound market a point slower in H1 2026); regulation D (the $127.28 per square centimetre skin-substitute cap from 1 Jan 2026, an 85 percent price cut, InnovaMatrix sales -94 percent to $2.5m in H1 2026, a 3.2 percent drag on group organic growth and 140 basis points on the H1 margin, $69m impairment; Medicare competitive bidding no earlier than 2028, a 30 percent retail cut, about 15 percent to manufacturers, 1 to 2 percent of group revenue, ostomy and continence about 60 percent of revenue; an FDA warning letter at Reynosa open to 2027); supply side C (80 percent of raw materials hedged for 2026 at about 3 percent inflation, the hedge rolling off in 2027 when each point above 3 percent costs $7 to 8m against $2 to 3m in 2026); macro C (currency: a 60 basis point margin headwind in H1 2026; GBP/USD at 1.39 would dilute sterling EPS by over 5 percent). Tailwinds: the company's own cycle B (trough in H1 2026, H2 guided 6 to 8 percent ex-InnovaMatrix, Infusion Care double-digit from 2027 on visible orders); disruption B (GLP-1 raises continuous-glucose-monitor use two to four times; the first patch-pump supply agreement signed in H1 2026). The sector's de-rating (eleven of fifteen peers at or below the 5th percentile of their ten-year P/E ranges) is a headwind on the multiple, not on earnings.
counter_case: In its strongest form, as the record carries it at the four Building Block heads: Convatec is a 5 percent-growth, number-three consumables maker in a sector whose multiples have re-based to 10 to 15x for good. Its second-act targets rest on the most back-end-loaded half-year it has ever set, a margin bridge the sell-side itself calls the most demanding in the company's history, a 380 basis point sequential step from 21.2 percent in H1 2026 to about 24.6 percent in H2 against a largest prior step of 190 basis points, to be delivered by a first-time chief executive from retail finance whose only prior chief executive role was a five-month interim at Halfords where margins were diluted, with no permanent chief financial officer (the incumbent resigned three months after presenting the plan) and no head of research and development, in the year its raw-material hedges roll off so that each point of inflation above 3 percent costs $7 to 8m. Its cash-flow metric was redefined the year growth capital expenditure doubled, turning a 27 percent decline on the legacy definition into 101 percent conversion. Over $500m of acquisitions produced $141m of impairments. A third of its shareholders voted against its pay while long-term incentive maxima rose to 525 percent of salary and restricted shares without performance conditions were introduced. The payer that took one line to zero with an 85 percent price cut returns in 2028 for the two categories that are 60 percent of revenue and for the double-margin 180 Medical channel that is the company's best asset, having acted twice in eighteen months (the cap; the FDA letter). The unanimous sell-side Buy, thirteen of thirteen with a mean target 46 percent above the price, against a multiple at the 2nd percentile of ten years that did not respond to a beat, a full write-off and a new buyback, is the crowd the framework says to fade: either the market knows something the sell-side does not, or this is the bland, uncut, consensus-long value case the framework was built to reject. The 11x multiple is the sector's new level, with Coloplast at 14.8x on a 27.5 percent margin and Smith & Nephew at 10.5x, so there is no re-rating to earn; the concern, a 5 percent grower with a hard year, is not transient; a 'Major CfC Clearing' would at least require estimates and guidance to have been cut, which they have not been, so buying an uncut, unanimously recommended stock at a low multiple is buying a value trap. At 11x with no re-rating the return is the earnings growth, 10 to 14 percent a year, a C at best and a D if the margin slips. The evidence for it is in the record: eleven of fifteen peer multiples at or below the 5th percentile of their ten-year ranges and still falling; the two closest peers cutting guidance on 4 Aug 2026; the finance seat; the forming cockroach (one actual problem and one possible); the 59 percent scoped-attribute share, one item short of the B line; the sandwich of nine individually tolerable weaknesses; wound ex-InnovaMatrix growing only 3.4 percent and ostomy 4.3 percent in H1 2026 against a 6 to 8 percent target that needs unprecedented ostomy share gains against Coloplast in a two-piece segment where the company has historically underperformed; the four-month update missing on Infusion Care phasing.

The record's response, at its full force too: it concedes the sector re-basing (the blend of 12.7x sits below the ten-year 'crash' band of 12.9x, not at the 16.6x median); the bridge's difficulty (65 percent, not 90); the scaffolding (a C on resources, a C on the 'Investment Case'); the count and the crowd; and that the case is bland on novelty. It holds because the bridge's arithmetic is flat costs on seasonal revenue, which the company has done before (H2 2025 was 23.2 percent); the InnovaMatrix drag of 140 basis points halves in H2 and vanishes in 2027 on the company's own base; the earnings and cash legs alone return about 14 percent a year at an unchanged multiple, so the downside on a clean miss is a D-rated return rather than a loss of capital (the mark-to-market to 10.0x is -14 percent, about 188p); the specific cause that took the shares from 259p to 193p is identifiable, at zero in the accounts, and hit the peers harder; the internal concern is dated and measurable rather than diffuse; and the multiple at the 2nd percentile already carries the miss the counter-case predicts. Where the record does not hold: if the sector's re-basing is permanent and the bridge is missed, the case is a C and should be parked; the February print decides which.
triggers: - The decisive print: FY2026 results on 23 Feb 2027. Alarm below 22.8 percent adjusted operating margin; invalidate below 22.5 percent; guidance at least 23.0 percent; consensus 23.0 percent; our modal 23.0 percent (about 24.6 percent in H2). A miss on the floor is at about 35 percent odds; it would cut this year's and next year's estimates at every house at once and make the cockroach pattern present.

- The second print: H1 2027 results in Aug 2027. Our modal 6.5 percent organic; alarm below 5.5 percent; invalidate below 4.5 percent; the price assumes about 5 percent; Natura Body slipping from Q2 2027 is an alarm.

- The last read before the print: the third-quarter trading update in Nov 2026. Alarm: ex-InnovaMatrix organic growth below 5.5 percent (invalidate below 5.0 percent for FY2026); Infusion Care orders slipping again; a sequential fall in adjusted gross margin, especially with rising ostomy volume (the false-friend test); InnovaMatrix below $5m.
- The finance seat: alarm if no chief financial officer is appointed by the 23 Feb 2027 print, or a further senior departure; our modal a public-markets finance officer before the print.

- The payer: a CMS proposal on ostomy or continence pricing in 2027 would change the view; alarm a manufacturer-level competitive-bidding cut above 15 percent; the record's modal is inaction before 2028 and a 1 to 2 percent revenue effect in 2028.

- The multiple: alarm below 10.5x 24-month-forward for three months; a Coloplast multiple back above its 25th percentile would move the record toward 16x; a further sector leg down would hold it at 11 to 12x whatever the company prints.
